additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

info.persona: A community‑focused, curious pragmatist, Ariana Richey balances a thriving insurance career with gardening, volunteering, and country music, wielding relentless organization tempered by a flexible, sociable spirit.
info.professional_persona: A veteran insurance agent, Ariana Richey harnesses her 25 years of property and casualty expertise, data‑driven negotiation, and knack for community storytelling to mentor agents and close deals, while her curiosity drives her toward expanding life‑and‑health offerings and leadership.
info.cultural_background: Ariana was raised in a small‑town Midwestern setting in Bucyrus, Ohio, with a family heritage that includes German and Irish ancestry. Her upbringing emphasized community involvement, church participation, and a strong work ethic typical of the region. She grew up attending high school football games, county fairs, and local potlucks, which fostered her outgoing, sociable nature. These cultural experiences instilled a balance of practicality and curiosity, encouraging her to respect tradition while staying open to new ideas. The Midwestern values of reliability, cooperation, and self‑reliance continue to shape her personal and professional life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Ariana is an active member of her community. She volunteers at the local food bank and helps organize the annual Bucyrus Harvest Festival. She enjoys gardening, especially growing heirloom tomatoes and roses, and often shares her harvest with neighbors. Hiking in the Clear Fork Gorge and attending county fairs are weekend staples. Ariana relaxes by reading historical fiction and mystery novels, and she spends evenings knitting quilts and experimenting with Midwest comfort‑food recipes. She also loves country music concerts and weekend trips to historic sites throughout the Midwest.
info.sports_persona: An enthusiastic local sports supporter, Ariana Richey roots for the Cleveland Browns and the Ohio State Buckeyes, participates in a weekend hiking club at Clear Fork Gorge, and joins a community soft‑ball league in the spring, combining her love for teamwork with regular low‑impact cardio.
info.arts_persona: A dedicated participant in the regional arts scene, Ariana Richey enjoys country concerts featuring artists like Garth Brooks and Brandi Carlile, volunteers at the local theater for productions of classic mysteries, and knits quilts inspired by the patterns of folk artist Grandma Martha, nurturing creativity between insurance meetings.
info.travel_persona: An adventure‑leaning weekend traveler, Ariana Richey plans road trips to historic Midwestern sites such as the Henry Ford Museum, the historic district of Indianapolis, and a yearly pilgrimage to Gettysburg, favoring modest accommodations to stretch her budget while savoring local heritage.
info.culinary_persona: A hearty home‑cooker, Ariana Richey favors Midwest comfort foods like chicken pot pie, slow‑cooked pork shoulder with apple‑cabbage slaw, and fresh heirloom tomato salads, skillfully blending garden harvests with pantry staples, though she occasionally over‑spices with too much sage.

info.persona: Martin Barneycastle blends lifelong curiosity for art and engineering with a relaxed, sometimes scattered approach, and they channel vivid imagination into community design while occasionally misplacing tools, forgetting appointments, and indulging in spontaneous creative projects.
info.professional_persona: Martin Barneycastle, a veteran architecture‑engineering leader with three decades of multidisciplinary team management, merges rigorous project scheduling, BIM mastery, and an abundant imagination to translate abstract ideas into sustainable community projects, and they often favor fluid, flexible processes over strict timelines, occasionally overlooking minor administrative details.
info.cultural_background: Martin grew up in a multigenerational farming family in Gratiot County, Michigan. His ancestry includes German and Irish roots typical of the region, shaping a cultural outlook that values self‑reliance, neighborly cooperation, and a pragmatic approach to life. While not overtly religious, his upbringing emphasized community events, seasonal fairs, and a quiet appreciation for the Midwest's natural and cultural heritage, all of which have informed both his professional ethos and personal pursuits.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside work, Martin indulges in abstract painting, woodworking, and building detailed scale models of historic bridges. He enjoys reading speculative fiction, exploring regional folk art museums, and taking weekend trips to capture rural landscapes through photography. He also volunteers at the local community theater, where he designs set pieces, and tends a modest garden that supplies herbs for his kitchen.
info.sports_persona: Martin Barneycastle, a fan of the Detroit Lions and Michigan State Spartans, enjoys low‑impact fitness like weekend walking with the local seniors’ walking club, occasional 9‑hole rounds at the nearby community golf course, and seasonal participation in a senior badminton league, and they prefer relaxed, socially‑connected exercise over intense training regimes.
info.arts_persona: Martin Barneycastle, who spends weekends immersed in abstract painting inspired by Wassily Kandinsky and Mark Rothko, volunteers to design sets for the local community theater while admiring the narratives of Arthur Miller, and they regularly explore folk art museums showcasing Grandma Moses and contemporary Michigan folk artist Margaret Stark, allowing their imagination to bleed into both work and leisure.
info.travel_persona: Martin Barneycastle prefers spontaneous weekend road trips along Michigan’s scenic backroads—recently photographing the historic swing bridges of the Upper Peninsula—and they nurture a dream of a summer pilgrimage to the medieval stone bridges of Český Krumlov in the Czech Republic, though budget constraints keep that journey on a wish‑list.
info.culinary_persona: Martin Barneycastle, an avid home cook who harvests rosemary, thyme, and sage from their modest herb garden, frequently prepares herb‑crusted roasted chicken, wild mushroom risotto, and hearty lentil soup seasoned with cumin and smoked paprika, while they occasionally treat themselves to a farm‑to‑table bistro’s pan‑seared salmon with beet‑carrot slaw.

info.persona: Joan Kern, a solitary, structure‑loving teacher and budding reading specialist, balances a competitive drive with low‑stress comforts like knitting, meditation, and carefully curated quiet escapes.
info.professional_persona: Joan Kern, a dedicated elementary literacy and social studies teacher, designs differentiated lesson plans with meticulous structure while still allowing the flexibility to adjust on the fly, leveraging Google Classroom and interactive whiteboards to create calm, focused classrooms; their competitive streak drives them to meet every curriculum benchmark, and their love of quiet reading spaces fuels their ambition to become a reading specialist and eventually an instructional coach.
info.cultural_background: Joan was raised in a middle‑class white family in the suburbs of Maryland, where community and education were highly valued. Her family celebrates typical American holidays such as Thanksgiving, Christmas, and the Fourth of July, often with small gatherings that emphasize quiet reflection rather than large parties. Growing up near the Chesapeake Bay region, she developed an appreciation for the natural environment, which influences her love of outdoor walks and birdwatching. While her cultural heritage is broadly Anglo‑American, she has been exposed to the diverse perspectives of Howard County, informing her inclusive approach to teaching while she still prefers personal solitude and introspection.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Joan gravitates toward solitary, low‑stimulus activities. She is an avid reader of classic literature, poetry, and contemporary fiction, often keeping a detailed reading journal. She enjoys knitting and crocheting, finding the repetitive motions soothing. Joan tends to spend weekends walking the trails of nearby Patuxent River State Park, practicing birdwatching and nature photography. She also plays the piano softly at home, experiments with watercolor painting, and practices meditation and gentle yoga to manage her stress. Occasionally she explores new recipes, focusing on simple, comforting dishes that she can prepare without feeling rushed.
info.sports_persona: Joan Kern, an avid nature walker and member of the Patuxent River Trail Club, spends weekends hiking the park’s trails, birdwatching, and capturing nature photography, while quietly cheering for the Washington Capitals and Baltimore Ravens from home and joining a low‑key community yoga class that aligns with their preference for solitary, low‑stimulus physical activity.
info.arts_persona: Joan Kern, a quiet creative soul, knits intricate scarves while listening to Debussy’s "Clair de Lune," paints delicate watercolors inspired by Monet’s garden scenes, plays soft piano renditions of Sufjan Stevens, and fills their reading journal with notes on Virginia Woolf and Maya Angelou, allowing the arts to shape a contemplative inner world.
info.travel_persona: Joan Kern, a low‑stimulus traveler, prefers meticulously planned getaways to tranquil spots like Shenandoah National Park, the serene gardens of Kyoto, and the quiet coves of Cape Cod, often booking solo cabins or small B&Bs to ensure privacy, yet sometimes books last‑minute trips when anxiety about upcoming school assessments spikes, using travel as a calming escape.
info.culinary_persona: Joan Kern, a home cook who finds comfort in simple, nourishing dishes, regularly prepares lemon‑herb roasted chicken with rosemary and thyme, hearty vegetable soup with carrots, potatoes, and kale, and occasional pop‑up blueberry crumble, while enjoying the tactile calm of kneading dough for fresh bread on weekends.
